title: God is love (1 John 4:7–12)
hookLine: whoever loves is born of God, for God is love
carry: love, and do what you will

cards: Church signs. Wedding programs. Bumper stickers.
A pillow stitched in a grandmother's living room. The same three words turn up on all of them, printed so often they can sound like wallpaper. But they began in this letter, and not as decoration.
The writer has just told his readers to test every spirit, to watch for voices that sound right and aren't. Right after that warning, he sets down the line all those signs borrowed.
Today, those three words where they actually live.

teach.b: In the King James Bible: "Beloved, let us love one another: for love is of God; and every one that loveth is born of God, and knoweth God." Love comes from God, the way light comes from the sun.
Then: "He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love." Notice the order.

teach.h: GOD IS LOVE, NOT LOVE IS GOD.
teach.b: God is love, not love is God; in the Greek, the grammar makes God the subject. The writer isn't saying that whatever we feel as love is divine. He's saying love belongs to God's very nature.
And what does that love look like?

teach.h: HE LOVED US FIRST, AND SENT HIS SON.
teach.b: "Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins." The love starts on God's side.
Propitiation is a heavy word: the offering that makes things right between us and God. Christians explain how that works in different ways, but they agree on the direction: love reaching first.
Then a startling line: "No man hath seen God at any time." Nobody.

teach.h: NO ONE HAS SEEN GOD. LOVE SHOWS HIM.
teach.b: Yet: "If we love one another, God dwelleth in us, and his love is perfected in us."
In the writer's telling, the unseen God is found, in a sense, wherever people love. Centuries later, Augustine preached a series of sermons on this letter.
In one he said, in Latin, dilige, et quod vis fac: love, and do what you will. He didn't mean anything goes. He meant that if love is the root within, what grows from it will be good.

how: 1 John 4:7–12 is read at some Christian weddings and funerals, and some churches teach children 'God is love' as a first, short summary of the faith.

o: the warm affection between close friends
self-giving love, the kind that reaches first

games.q: nobody has ever seen God, the letter admits. so where, according to the writer, can God's love be seen?
games.why: "If we love one another, God dwelleth in us, and his love is perfected in us."

practice: Think of someone you love with a few conditions attached, if they'd only call more, if they'd say sorry first, and picture their face.
Gently set the conditions down one at a time, like taking stones out of your pockets, and notice what's left. If you pray, hold their name before God, just as they are.

wordCard.voice: Agape. Greek for self-giving love: First John's claim that God is love, not that love is God, and that love belongs to God's very nature.

orig.note: Greek: love, especially self-giving love. the word in ho theos agapē estin, God is love.

carryVoice: Your line: love, and do what you will. Three words, back where they began. Take care until tomorrow.
